content:
The image shows a corn leaf with:
- Numerous small, round to oval pustules scattered across the leaf surface
- Pustules appear orange/tan/rust-colored
- Distributed densely across both sides of the midrib
- The leaf is otherwise green and healthy-looking
- Some purple/reddish discoloration along the midrib area

The small, round, scattered orange/rust-colored pustules densely distributed across the corn leaf surface are characteristic of **Common Rust** (*Puccinia sorghi*). These circular to elongated, cinnamon-brown uredia scattered across both leaf surfaces are the hallmark symptom. Southern Rust pustules tend to be more orange and concentrated on the upper surface, while Common Rust has darker, more scattered pustules on both surfaces — matching what's seen here.
